instruction: Place both cups upright on the tray, then let go.

outcome.real_measurement: Rationale: 'upright' = the cup's own up axis (model local +y, which is world +z at reset; the released code wrongly tests local z against world -x) within 15 deg of vertical, averaged over the last 1 s. A cup standing on a flat tray is at ~0-2 deg; lying on its side is ~90 deg; 15 deg leaves room for model asymmetry and the tray floor. Real world: fiducial or fitted cylinder axis from a calibrated RGB-D camera, angle to the table normal.
As for cup 1 (cup 2 = 021_cup model 6, local +y up).

Rationale: 'on the tray' = cup xy inside the tray's footprint (world AABB of its collision mesh) AND cup-tray contact force > 0.05 N, in every one of the last 20 control steps (1 s). Real world: top camera segments tray and cup base (cup-base centroid inside the tray polygon) plus a scale/load cell under the tray showing the cup's weight.

Rationale: settled = both cups at rest (mean of max cup speed over the last 1 s <= 2 cm/s), so a cup still rolling/sliding is not judged. Real world: frame differencing of the tracked cup poses over 1 s.

counterexamples.name: place_then_knock_over
counterexamples.description: official placement, then each cup is swept over (E1)

source.released_code_predicate: success = both cups' xy within 0.15 m of the tray centre; is_cup_*_upright (local z vs world -x/+x) computed, unused

notes: released = neither cup is_grasping by either arm over the final 10 control steps.
